BiblicalUsage: Hammedatha is named as the father of Haman the Agagite, the enemy who plotted to destroy all the Jews in the days of Esther. His ten sons were hanged with him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the father's name is kept because the hatred was inherited: Haman was the son of Hammedatha, an Agagite, and the old enmity of Amalek came back in his generation — and God turned it back on his own head.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
